RustScenic signed-activity confirmation, frozen 7 November 2026

Question
Does preserving and separately normalising positive and negative TF-target
programmes improve classification on an external cohort, at low scoring cost?
This tests activity representation, not improved causal or enhancer prediction.
No new inference, topic fitting, motif selection or parameter search is performed.

Independent biological confirmation
Kang et al. 2018, GSE96583, unstimulated PBMCs from eight donors. These donors
are separate from the GSE194122 BMMC networks used to develop the correction.
Use every control cell in the frozen scverse data object. Exclude stimulated
cells by condition, not by outcomes. X must contain integer counts whose library
totals agree exactly with the source's nCount_RNA metadata, not SCT totals.
Intersect gene identifiers with the original 5,000-gene BMMC vocabulary, without
using cell labels or expression variability. Keep original network memberships.
Report coverage and zero-score signatures; do not drop unfavourable TFs or donors.
Signatures with less than 80% of their original targets measured score zero for
both scorers. Keep their TF columns and report them. This shared coverage rule
prevents a native/reference mismatch in handling missing genes.

Reuse all 12 frozen BMMC outputs: two methods, 5,000 and 20,000 training cells,
three inference seeds. No external donor contributed to those network fits.
Primary: same common TF roster per original method pair, one feature per TF,
shared pySCENIC AUCell scorer, positive-target AUC minus negative-target AUC.
Compare corrected RustScenic vs corrected SCENIC+ and corrected vs original
RustScenic. Keep original unsigned endpoints for both methods. The 20,000-cell
networks are primary; 5,000-cell networks test the residual small-sample gap.

Use fixed StandardScaler plus balanced L2 logistic regression (C=1, lbfgs,
max_iter=2000), leaving out each external donor in turn. Fit the classifier and
scaling only on the other seven external donors. External labels train the
fold-specific classifier only; no labels modify the frozen networks or scoring.
Report macro-F1, balanced accuracy, per-class confusion matrices, convergence,
unseen labels and all-TF secondary results. Average seeds within each donor
before paired bootstrap intervals. Eight donors, not 24 independent replicates.
Do not introduce a post-result non-inferiority margin or automatic paper-ready
verdict. Independent cohort confirmation is not proof of TF-target edge truth.

Controls, fixed before outcomes
Repeat common-TF comparisons with Rust AUCell for the Rust networks to confirm
the correction also works with the shipped engine. Report matched-TF expression,
training-fold expression PCA50, five size-matched random gene-set controls for
seed777/20,000 cells and ten within-training-donor label permutations for that
primary comparison. Preserve positive/negative group sizes, observed gene
coverage and disjointness in random controls.
Check SPI1 activity in monocytes, PAX5/EBF1 in B cells, TCF7 in CD4/CD8 T cells;
report missing signatures, never count them as successful negatives.
Do not locally calculate external-cohort classifier scores during package QA.
QA uses synthetic data and already inspected BMMC cells; new cohort checks are
limited to schema, count integrity, gene coverage and donor identities.

Speed and memory
Reuse the existing real 817,740-cell HDMA RNA matrix and all three seed networks.
For each seed, run original union and corrected signed gene scoring for each
method in separate fresh processes, sequentially on the same 16-core node.
Use identical 4,096-cell blocks for both modes and scorers, with the same input,
output dtype and uncompressed HDF5 output format. Alternate mode/method order by
seed. These are paired measurements of the affected scoring/export stage, not
a fresh full-workflow head-to-head. They must not replace original full-pipeline
timings or be used to claim a new end-to-end speedup by adding unrelated peaks.
The 1.3-million-cell RNA inference comparison is unchanged by this multiome fix.
Capture score, combine, read and write timings plus whole-process elapsed time,
sampled process-tree PSS/RSS, environment/source hashes and output checksums.
Retain full scores on HPC; return a fixed 10,000-cell sample, summaries and logs.
No cells are simulated, repeated or upsampled to create atlas-scale input.

Resources and restart
One preparation job: 4 cores, 32 GB, 2 h. Six independent biology jobs: 16 cores,
64 GB, 24 h, maximum two concurrently. Three atlas jobs: 16 cores, 128 GB, 24 h,
maximum one concurrently; per scoring process guard 110 GB / 5 h. These are
conservative allocation limits, not runtime forecasts. LSF memory requests
use per-core rusage and total -M, following the audited Minerva convention.
Require 80 GiB free scratch. Do not change existing runtimes or old results.
Completed checksummed tasks are reused. A deliberate --resume only resubmits
failed/incomplete work after earlier jobs end; normal start prevents duplicates.
Collection runs even after failures and reports missing results explicitly.
Everything necessary except the existing runtime and atlas matrix is bundled.
